title: 5 ETFs I'm BUYING Before 2027
creator: Mark Roussin CPA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions.
summary: Mark Roussin CPA lays out five ETFs he is accumulating before 2027 after the correction and Monday's relief rally, with the fear and greed index at 9 on Friday and 17 now. His theme is restructuring to upgrade portfolio quality while fear is highest, quoting Buffett on being greedy when others are fearful. QQQM (Invesco Nasdaq 100, 0.15% fee) is his foundational tech exposure, up 7.5% over 12 months with the top 10 holdings near 50% of the fund. SOXX (iShares Semiconductor) targets the beaten-down chip sector, down nearly 40% from its June peak; he prefers it over SMH for its larger AMD weighting, with AMD the top holding. SCHD (Schwab US Dividend Equity) provides balance, up 24% year to date against about 6% for the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500; he added on 19 November. XLG (Invesco S&P 500 Top 50) increases mega-cap exposure, with Apple and Nvidia each about 12%, and he plans to layer in rather than go all in. GDX (VanEck Gold Miners) is the tactical play, drawing a 2018 parallel in which miners rose about 20% from September to December while equities fell, and explaining miners' operating leverage with a $3,000 gold versus $1,800 cost example; GDX is down nearly 40% from its 52-week high. He warns the five overlap and that position sizing matters. Calls: QQQM and SOXX BUY (first tracked); SCHD, XLG and GDX BUY (reiterations).
